parts:
Hello,

I got two errors:

1) by running a joint model with "big" data:

I got it also with not so big simulated data. If I click on Ignore (or actually ignore it and don't click on anything) then it continues to run. The error appeared a couple of more times but at the end I got a model.
At a linux server (24gb) for the real (bigger than the simulations) data I got malloc() problem. So probably it's a memory issue (without seeing RAM increased in Windows, 12gb) also since 13780 is a reallocation(?).
INLA build date .........: Thu 18 Jul 11:30:55 CEST 2013
R version 3.0.1 (2013-05-16)
Platform: x86_64-w64-mingw32/x64 (64-bit)

Shall I trust the model I get after ignoring the message?
If yes, is it possible to say from the inla() call to ignore it so that I can do it on the server as well?

2) by running a loop of -simple not big- binomial models with a spatial-spde effect I am getting:
Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() :
.....
In addition: Warning messages:
1: running command 'C:\Windows\system32\cmd.exe /c @"C:\Users\Alex\AppData\Local\Temp\RtmpKKYEP5\file15245efc1e93.BAT"' had status 5
2: In shell(paste("@", shQuote(bat.file), sep = ""), wait = TRUE) :
  '@"C:\Users\Alex\AppData\Local\Temp\RtmpKKYEP5\file15245efc1e93.BAT"' execution failed with error code 5

Running one by one the models I get no error so the verbose didn't show me anything to post here.
By putting Sys.sleep(4) or a stupid and big calculation after every model the loop goes further but not always finishes.
At the server some loops finished and for one specifically I got an malloc() again, although all models can be run at a desktop computer.
Is there a way/command to calculate the RAM needed before running a model?


Best,
Alex
